messages:
maria: Heads-up — sudden capacity drop in us-west1 GPU pool, started ~now. Approx 18% GPUs unavailable, tail latencies up ~350ms. Telemetry shows NVLINK and PCIe AER counters spiking alongside device resets. Auto-drains are kicking in. Anyone on it?

ash: I see the same on the cluster health dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/us-west1/gpu-health — link CRCs and link flaps on multiple racks, heatmaps point to rack-r13 and rack-r21.

devon: Opening vendor ticket RWD-7891 and alerting colo support. Can we route more traffic away from us-west1 while we triage?

maria: Done — pushed temporary routing weight shift (us-west1 -> 60%, us-east1 -> 40%) for latency-critical traffic. Also started manual drain of suspicious nodes in rack-r13.

leo: Pulled kernel logs from rack-r13-07, snippets below:
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:81:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus
[ 1234.568001] pcieport 0000:00:1c.7: AER: multiple Corrected error received: ID 0000
[ 1234.568123] nvidia 0000:81:00.0: GPU reset: reason=GPC_FATAL
```

ash: That looks like link/PCIe flapping. Can we check driver/firmware versions across affected hosts? Also check thermal channels in case of power/PSU issues.

devon: Doing an inventory: affected nodes show nvidia-driver 535.86, firmware tag fw-2024-07-12. I've attached full logs to the ticket and uploaded to S3: s3://rwd-logs/gpu-health/1987654321/ (structured logs + dmesg + nvidia-smi -q).

infra-bot: Auto-drain rule "gpu-soft-ecc-rate>0.5%" triggered for 12 nodes, initiated at 1987654360.

ops-oncall: Heads up — provisioner queue length is 42 right now, estimate ~12m to spin up additional GPU VMs. If we keep fallback routing we will see cost increase.

maria: Mitigation actions: 1) shift partial traffic away from us-west1, 2) bump reserved pool for latency-critical to 20% (was 10%), 3) disable batching for critical routes to reduce chance of amplified tail latency, 4) start controlled canary rollback of driver on one rack. Cost implications acknowledged.

ash: Vendor (cc @vendor-nvidia) — any known regressions with 535.x that could cause NVLINK CRC spikes?

vendor-nvidia: Thanks for the ping. We're seeing a few reports with 535.* in the field that correlate with increased link CRC and unexpected resets on NVLINK topologies. Please collect `nvidia-smi -q -d LINK,PERF` and full dmesg; we'll correlate serials and firmware.

devon: Logs uploaded, ticket RWD-7891 updated with serials and dmesg. Also annotated nodes to hold auto-drain for canary testing: `fleetctl node annotate rack-r13-07 maintenance=investigate`.

leo: Performed a small canary rollback to driver 530.41 on rack-r13-05 and observed NVLINK CRC errors drop to zero over 30m:
```
Driver Version: 530.41
NVLINK CRC Errors: 0 (last 30m)
```

maria: Good signal. Plan: roll driver back to 530.41 on affected racks in a controlled rollout, hold auto-drain on canary and rollback candidates so we don't keep losing capacity mid-investigation, and coordinate with vendor for firmware patch.

infra-bot: Change request CR-4021 created to roll driver to 530.41 in us-west1-gpu-pool; approvals pending.

ops-oncall: Cost note: estimated incremental spend ~$12k in next 24h if we maintain partial fallback + extra reserved nodes. Approving short-term spend to preserve SLOs.

devon: Vendor response: likely regression in 535.x series; they recommend rollback and firmware validation. ETA for firmware patch ~6-8h. See internal vendor link: https://support.nvidia.internal/issue/535-regression (internal doc).

maria: Assignments: devon -> vendor coordination and logs; ash -> rollback orchestration and CR follow-through; leo -> postmortem draft and telemetry collection. Incident bridge scheduled at 1987654500. Escalate to #incidents if latency SLOs breach.

sre-bot: Incident INC-2026 created (P2). Bridge at 1987654500. Runbook attached: gpu-fabric-degradation-v1.

ash: Proposal: stop auto-drain only for canary nodes during rollback, keep auto-drain for nodes with hardware indicated by LED/hardware faults. Approve?

ops-oncall: Approve temporary hold on auto-drain for canaries only. Hardware-fault nodes still auto-drain.

maria: Applying auto-drain rule updates now.

leo: Noted two units with persistent ECC counters and hardware error LED lit; filed replace orders with colo (RMA-1293).

devon: Vendor will push firmware patch once we provide a minimal repro bundle; in the meantime we continue rollbacks.

maria: Thanks team. We'll reconvene on the bridge. :thumbsup:
